newsitem.title: KENYA: 80 Rwandans arrested in Kenyan capital.
newsitem.headline: 80 Rwandans arrested in Kenyan capital.

text.p: Kenyan police have rounded up 80 Rwandans in Nairobi a day after seven Rwanda genocide suspects were arrested and handed to the U.N. genocide tribunal, a senior U.N. tribunal official said on Sunday.

"Eighty Rwandans were arrested by the Kenyan police on Saturday, but it has nothing to do with us (the U.N. Rwanda tribunal). They will probably be released after a few days," said the official who declined to be identified.
A senior Kenya police officer denied on Sunday any Rwandans had been detained.

Seven suspects including Jean Kambanda, Rwanda's prime minister during the 1994 genocide, were arrested by Kenyan police working with tribunal officials in a series of dawn raids in Nairobi on Friday. They were transferred to tribunal headquarters in Arusha, northern Tanzania.
Kenya police, contacted by Kenya newspapers, denied they played a part in the Friday arrests.

The arrests and the indictment of two of the suspects represent the biggest swoop so far by the ICTR set up to bring to justice the leading architects of the 1994 genocide of an estimated 800,000 Tutsis and some politically moderate Hutus.

Rwanda's Vice-President Major-General Paul Kagame discussed the question of Hutus living in Nairobi with Kenya President Daniel arap Moi during a visit on Wednesday he said patched up relations between the two states.
Kenya's decision to grant safe haven to prominent Hutus connected to the regime of Rwanda's late president Juvenal Habyrimana soured relations with the Rwanda government which came to power in 1994.
